Business logic, bug and security review otherwise clean, but one finding crosses the medium bar. findings=[{"file":"test/google-routes.test.ts","line_or_range":"207-217","concern":"The 'is absent from the connection status response' test — the suite's only test asserting the credential never leaves the Worker via GET /api/google/connection — wraps its sole assertion in `if (res.status === 200) { expect(await res.text()).not.toContain(\"stored-refresh-token\"); }`. If the route ever regresses to erroring on every call, this test would pass vacuously without ever inspecting a response body, silently losing the one test that guards the credential-never-leaves invariant for this endpoint. No other test in the suite independently proves GET /connection returns 200 with a real body when a connection is seeded.","severity":"medium"}]. Everything else checked clean: the refresh token is never logged (no console.* call in any of the three new production files) and never appears in any response body — `refuse()` in oauth-callback.ts is called only with static Portuguese string literals at every call site (grep confirms zero interpolation of `exchanged`/token values), and `toGoogleConnectionDto` in dto.ts maps exactly {connected, connectedAt, scope} with no refreshToken field, matching `GoogleConnectionDto` in api.ts field-by-field. `crypto.randomUUID()` is a CSPRNG-backed v4 UUID (122 bits of entropy) under workerd, cryptographically adequate for a single-use nonce; the 10-minute TTL is reasonable and consistently applied in both google.ts's connect handler and the schema's CHECK requiring expires_at > created_at (that CHECK guards TTL positivity at write time, not the runtime now-vs-expiresAt comparison in isNonceUsable, so there is no boundary inconsistency between the two — isNonceUsable's `expiresAt > now` is a closed-boundary check evaluated purely in application code). DELETE /api/google/connection's local deletion is genuinely unconditional: revokeToken() in client.ts never throws (both its try/catch and its non-throwing on non-2xx are structural), and the route computes `revoked` before the unconditional `db.delete(googleConnections)` call with no conditional branching around the delete.

Sub-agent (code-reviewer-semantic) finding, corroborated independently in this review's own race-condition analysis of oauth-callback.ts: plan Task 7 states the refresh token must be stored and the nonce marked consumed 'in the SAME operation so replaying the identical URL falls into the rejection path'. The implementation instead performs two separate, non-atomic awaited statements — `await db.insert(googleConnections)...onConflictDoUpdate(...)` followed by a distinct `await db.update(oauthStates).set({ consumedAt: new Date() })...` — with no db.batch()/transaction wrapping either statement. D1 (per the plan's own framing) offers no cross-statement transaction here, so a worker termination between the two awaits would leave the credential stored but the nonce unconsumed, permitting a subsequent replay of the identical callback URL to attempt a second exchangeCode call rather than being refused locally at the nonce-check stage — a narrower, provider-mitigated version of the same gap (Google's own authorization-code single-use semantics would still reject the second exchange in the common case), but a literal deviation from the task's 'same operation' wording that the review is required to record rather than wave through.

The attempt-1 finding is fixed, independently re-verified by direct inspection of the current file (not the coordinator's description alone) plus a second dispatch of the code-reviewer-semantic sub-agent against the updated oauth-callback.ts. Lines 92-104 now read `await db.batch([ db.insert(googleConnections).values({...}).onConflictDoUpdate({...}), db.update(oauthStates).set({ consumedAt: new Date() }).where(eq(oauthStates.id, state)), ]);` — both statement builders are constructed as plain (unawaited) query-builder objects and handed to a single `db.batch([...])` call with no `await` separating their construction; `batch()` is D1's documented cross-statement atomicity primitive (the plan's own Risks section already noted D1 has no multi-statement transaction, and `batch()` is the closest available primitive). This satisfies the plan Task 7 wording 'mark the nonce consumed in the SAME operation' literally rather than approximately: a worker termination can no longer land between 'credential stored' and 'nonce consumed' as two independently-committed states. The route's earlier ordering — no outbound call and no write before isNonceUsable passes — is unchanged and re-confirmed by direct read of lines 42-70: the `db.select().from(oauthStates)` read at line 57 is the only DB touch before the isNonceUsable gate at line 68, and it is a read, not a write; exchangeCode (the only outbound call) is not invoked until line 79, strictly after the gate.

Ruling on all four disputed edits against test/oauth-callback.test.ts, test/google-routes.test.ts and test/google-oauth.test.ts, each verified directly against the repo rather than taken on the implementer's word. (1) mintNonce fixture (test/oauth-callback.test.ts): DISPUTE_UPHELD_TEST_WRONG. The approved fixture inserted createdAt=now, expiresAt=now-1 to represent an expired nonce. src/worker/db/schema.ts:317 carries check("oauth_states_expiry_after_creation", sql`${t.expiresAt} > ${t.createdAt}`) — added in this SAME phase's Task 2, which the approved plan text itself mandates ("Add a CHECK that expires_at > created_at"). Under that CHECK the original INSERT throws before the test body's assertion is ever reached; the fixture encoded a database state production can never produce, since an expired nonce is necessarily one whose creation is also in the past. The edit changes no assertion, only derives createdAt as one TTL before expiresAt. This is a plan-vs-test internal contradiction the test-writer introduced, not a PRD ambiguity or a case for relaxing the CHECK — the CHECK is the correct, plan-mandated, ADR-0006-style structural invariant and must stay. Test was wrong; upheld. (2) google-routes.test.ts leaked-token guard (the R-SEM fix): DISPUTE_UPHELD_TEST_WRONG. Confirmed via git diff HEAD that the approved test wrapped its sole assertion in `if (res.status === 200) { expect(...).not.toContain("stored-refresh-token") }` — a vacuous guard that would pass even if the route regressed to erroring on every call, silently losing the suite's only guard on PRD AC-4's 'no row modified'/token-secrecy property (GoogleConnectionDto never carries the token, per Files-to-Change row 6 and dto.ts's field-by-field mapping). The approved test's actual enforced behavior ('assert nothing unless status happens to be 200') contradicts AC-3/AC-4's plain reading, which requires the token never leaves the Worker, unconditionally. The edit removes the conditional, asserts status 200 unconditionally, and adds two tests pinning the DTO's exact key set — a strengthening, not a weakening, and no existing assertion was altered or deleted. Upheld. General pipeline ruling requested by the coordinator: a reviewer's own R-SEM finding recorded in a prior standard-mode CHANGES_REQUESTED entry is NOT itself authorization to edit a test. It is a report, not a grant of Edit authority — accepting 'the reviewer implied it' as self-executing authorization would let an implementer bypass R-X on any test-quality complaint without independent arbitration, defeating D17's purpose. The correct path, and the one actually followed here, is: R-SEM flags the defect -> CHANGES_REQUESTED -> implementer treats the test itself as the obstacle -> implementer files TEST_CONTRACT_DISPUTE -> reviewer arbitrates on the merits. This dispute followed that path correctly; the arbitration verdict is the authorization, not the earlier R-SEM note. (3) and (4) prettier-only formatting on test/google-oauth.test.ts and test/google-routes.test.ts: verified genuinely semantics-free. Diffs inspected token-by-token — both hunks are pure line-wrap/re-flow (an import statement reflowed to one line; an awaited chained call reflowed across lines) with identical identifiers, identical call arguments, zero added or removed tokens beyond whitespace/newlines. Independently confirmed both approved (git show HEAD) versions of these files FAIL `npx prettier --check`, and the current working-tree versions PASS it — so `npm run check` (the plan's own mandatory Level 1 Validation Command) could not have exited 0 without these edits. Ruled DISPUTE_UPHELD_TEST_WRONG by the closest available category, since these are not genuine test-content disputes at all — but flagging explicitly, as the coordinator asked: R-X's `git diff --name-only -- <pathspec>` check is content-blind by construction (D17/this agent's own Phase 2 definition), so it cannot distinguish a semantics-free reflow from a substantive change. This produces a structural tension for ANY phase whose test-writer-approved suite is not already prettier-clean: Level 1 (mandatory, gates APPROVED) and R-X (mandatory, straight-fail, no grace period) cannot both be satisfied without a test-glob-matching diff appearing, and no clause in D17 or the R-X definition anticipates this. Recording this as a pipeline finding for docs/decisions.md consideration: either the test-writer's suite must be prettier-clean at approval time (shifting the burden upstream), or R-X should gain a narrow, structurally-verifiable formatting-only exception (e.g. AST/token-stream equality against the pre-edit blob), because as written, the current specification leaves no compliant path for a phase in this state. Overall dispute verdict: DISPUTE_UPHELD_TEST_WRONG. Two of the four edits are unambiguous fixture/assertion corrections against the approved-but-defective test content (impossible precondition; vacuous assertion contradicting AC-3/AC-4's plain reading). The remaining two are non-semantic formatting compelled by the plan's own Level 1 gate, verified byte-for-byte content-equivalent to the pre-edit approved test files, and are folded into the same upheld disposition rather than rejected, with the pipeline tension flagged above for the record.
